title: Col. John Todd of Lexington
summary: Lawyer John Todd (1750–1782) served Kentucky County, rode with George Rogers Clark, and became Fayette’s first militia colonel and a Lexington trustee.
bodyMarkdown:
Pennsylvania-born lawyer John Todd (1750–1782) reached Kentucky around 1775, sat in Virginia’s legislature for Kentucky County, rode with George Rogers Clark to Kaskaskia and Vincennes, and was named civil commandant of Illinois County. Back home he became Fayette’s first militia colonel (Boone as lieutenant colonel) and a Lexington trustee who deeded land to the young town.

After Bryan Station’s siege he led the pursuit that ended at Blue Licks on August 19, 1782, where he was killed at 32; brother Levi helped bury the dead. Todd County (1819) still carries his name—great-uncle of Mary Todd Lincoln.
Source: [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Todd_(Virginia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Todd_(Virginia))
